brief.headline: Push for ₹290/kg on laminates (matching Shrinath) and offer to pay 15 days faster in return for a small cut — they're loss-making and carry a lot of debt, so they value cash, but tread carefully to avoid tipping them over

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹290/kg on the three big Electral laminate SKUs
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Shrinath Roto Pack ₹290/kg for identical items (LM ELECTRAL MD 21.80g LS 07, LM ELECTRAL UD 4.4g LS 05, LM ELECTRAL MD 21.80g LS 08); GLS charges ₹295/kg — a 1.7% gap. The open market for pharma ORS sachet laminate sits at ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), so their ₹295/kg is at the top of fair; ₹290/kg is still fair and is a price we already pay elsewhere

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (15 days after receipt instead of 30) if they cut price by about 1–2%
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹9.49 L of cash for us, but they borrow money at about 10.96%, so 15 days early is worth roughly 0.5% of the invoice to them — a smaller saving than the ₹5/kg price cut we want, but it sweetens the deal and gives them cash when they need it (they made a loss of ₹-23.68 Cr in FY2024-25 and carry debt of ₹208.21 Cr)

brief.financialLeverage: GLS made a loss in FY2024-25 (₹-23.68 Cr net, -3.4% margin) and carries high debt (2.15x their own cash, total ₹208.21 Cr). Their overall money-health score is 2/10 and they sit in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.68). They also have severe legal cases, GST filing delays and EPF payment delays. Our ₹2.31 Cr spend is only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so we're not a make-or-break customer. Push gently: lead with the ₹290/kg benchmark (a price we already pay) and faster payment as a carrot, but don't squeeze so hard you lose supply — have a backup ready.

evidence.point: They carry a lot of debt
evidence.figure: ₹208.21 Cr total debt, 2.15x their own cash

evidence.point: Their money-health score is very weak
We pay Shrinath ₹290/kg for the same three Electral laminate SKUs

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter (already a tiny FDC supplier) with ₹2755.75 Cr revenue and C health (58/100) — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant (₹16492.00 Cr revenue, C health 46/100) that makes both film and converts it — can second-source at scale

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, specialises in pharma blister and sachet laminates (₹222.04 Cr revenue, D health 31/100) — strong second source for Electral sachets

risks: They made a loss of ₹-23.68 Cr in FY2024-25 and sit in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.68) — pushing too hard on price could tip them into serious trouble and kill your supply; keep the ask reasonable and have a backup qualified
They have severe legal cases, GST filing delays and EPF payment delays (all flagged in their risk profile) — a sign of operational stress; monitor deliveries closely
Their credit rating is only IVR BBB- / Stable and their money-health score is 2/10 — don't put all your laminate eggs in this basket; split volume with a healthier alternate like Huhtamaki or UFLEX
We're only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue — we have almost no volume leverage, so the ask must be rooted in fairness (matching a price we already pay) rather than muscle
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about bringing your laminate price in line with what we pay Shrinath — ₹290 a kilo — and in return we can pay you faster, which should help with cash flow.
